title: AuditPack: self-serve evidence bundles and residency-aware retention controls
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary:
Deliver a self-serve "AuditPack" feature that lets customers assemble, verify, and export audit evidence bundles for compliance requests (DPA, SOC/ISO, data residency checks). AuditPack combines questionnaire exports, configuration snapshots, residency proofs, retention policy attestations, and cryptographic timestamping so a customer or auditor can validate Redwood's state at the time of the request.

Goals and scope:
- Provide UI and API to generate a repeatable evidence bundle containing: questionnaire responses (structured), DPA clause mapping, exportable logs (access and change history), storage residency manifests, retention policy snapshots, KMS key usage attestations, and optional on-prem/VPC deployment manifests.
- Introduce retention settings UI allowing org admins to set per-tenant and per-route TTLs and residency constraints, with clear defaults and override paths.
- Automate packaging so evidence bundles are reproducible and auditable (includes chain-of-custody metadata and SHA256 hashes for attachments).
- Support both ad-hoc bundles (for customer requests) and scheduled periodic exports (for retention audits).

Non-goals:
- Do not integrate with third-party governance platforms in v1 (will expose export hooks for integration in v2).
- No live remediation of retention settings (enforcement happens in storage layer via scheduled jobs).

Acceptance criteria:
- Customer can create an AuditPack via Console and API and download a ZIP containing all artifacts and a top-level manifest.json with hashes and timestamps.
- Residency manifest includes region-of-record per dataset, signed by Redwood service identity, and references to underlying infra resources (region, bucket names masked to org id).
- Retention UI allows setting global default + per-route overrides and displays effective retention with warnings when shorter than legal minimums.
- Evidence generation takes <30s for small bundles (metadata-only) and streams progress for large exports.
- Legal/Privacy signoff obtained and KMS interactions documented.

Implementation outline:
Phase 1 (MVP):
- Backend: export service that queries config DB, audit log store, and residency metadata store; builds manifest; zips artifacts; signs manifest with service KMS key.
- Console: single-screen AuditPack builder with template selection (DPA, SOC-2 readiness, custom questionnaire), preview, and export button.
- API: POST /v1/auditpacks -> starts export job, GET /v1/auditpacks/{id} -> status + download url.
- Retention UI: add per-tenant retention policy page and per-route override modal; store policies in policy-store and expose to runtime via policy cache.

Phase 2 (hardening):
- Scheduled export jobs, expiry of generated bundles after configurable window, RBAC for who can generate/download bundles, enhanced chain-of-custody logs.
- Add function to include redaction filters for PII in exported request/response logs.

Trade-offs and decisions considered:
- Signing manifests centrally vs. per-tenant: chose central service KMS for MVP to avoid per-tenant key management complexity; roadmap includes tenant-key signing for enterprise customers.
- Export performance vs. completeness: stream metadata first, allow selective inclusion of heavy artifacts (full logs) to avoid timeouts.
- UI complexity: provide first-class templates rather than fully custom questionnaire builder to reduce scope.

Dependencies:
- Policy-store & retention enforcement hooks (ENG-3845)
- Existing DPA clause mapping project (PM-12120) for clause IDs and canonical text
- KMS/HSM integration for manifest signing (security team)

Success metrics:
- Reduction in manual compliance requests handled by Solutions/SE by 60% in first quarter post-launch.
- Time-to-first-bundle <= 5 minutes from template selection for standard templates.
- >90% of bundles requested via API without manual Ops intervention.

Risks / mitigations:
- Legal scope creep: engage Legal at milestone gate and require explicit signoff before exposing DPA clause text.
- Data leakage via exported logs: default to metadata-only exports; require explicit opt-in to include raw request payloads; provide PII redaction filters.
- Long-running exports impact on runtime: run exports from offline replicas and rate-limit concurrent exports per org.

Rollout plan:
- Alpha: internal red-team + 3 enterprise customers (manual enablement) for feedback on artifacts and manifest format.
- Beta: opt-in for all customers with quota limits and retention for generated bundles.
- GA: enabled per-plan with SLA on availability of export service and auditability metrics in Console.

Artifacts and references:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPLIANCE/AuditPack+Design
- Design mocks: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AuditPackMocks (see console/export flow)
- Example package spec: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auditpack-spec

2025-11-05 - Legal review (Maya Li): Requested that DPA clause exports must include versioning and redaction guidance. Flag: cannot expose raw customer IDs in exported manifests without masking.
2026-01-22 - Security (Diego Ramos): KMS signing approach approved for MVP. Action: generate KMS key rotation plan and define service principal with restricted permissions.
2026-02-16 - Ravi Patel: Customer research with 5 SOC-ready customers shows high value for scheduled periodic bundles; adding as Phase 2 priority. Captured in roadmap.

2026-03-08 - QA (Aleena Verma): Ran integration test for small bundle export; manifest generation and hash validation passed. Large-log streaming job still flaky under load; ENG ticket opened ENG-55321.
